Chapter 5: The Rewards of Mastery and the Cost of Settling for Average
Have you ever noticed how the world just doesn’t reward mediocrity?
No matter which field you look at, it’s almost always the best who enjoy the biggest benefits. That could mean more money, a stronger reputation, or even just that deep sense of personal satisfaction.
It’s not really about fairness—it's simply how people work.
We’re drawn to the best products, the best services, and the best experiences. And, let’s be honest, we’re usually willing to pay extra for them.
This is what makes pushing through those tough, uncertain times—the dip—so worthwhile.
Here’s the thing: the difference between average and the best isn’t just a small step up. It’s an entirely different world.
When you reach the top, you start attracting more opportunities, you can charge higher prices, and you just feel more fulfilled. The truth is, rewards aren’t spread out evenly. They’re stacked up at the top.
Now, settling for average? That’s a fast track to frustration.
The middle of the pack is crowded, it’s fiercely competitive, and honestly, it’s easy to be overlooked there. If you give up when things get tough—or if you spread yourself too thin across a bunch of different things—you rarely end up with meaningful success.
Sure, you might be working hard, but your efforts get scattered.
Mastery isn’t supposed to be easy.
There’s a reason the dip is tough: it weeds out everyone but the most committed. That’s why being the best is so valuable—because it’s rare. And that scarcity? That’s what creates those outsized rewards.
So, how do you make the most of this?
First, focus on becoming the best in one area instead of just being good enough at lots of things.
See the dip as a necessary part of your journey, not a signal to give up.
Resist the urge to spread yourself too thin. The real secret to mastery isn’t doing everything—it’s going deep, not just broad.
And remember, letting go of average pursuits frees up your time, energy, and focus for what truly matters.
Settling for average doesn’t just mean missing out on big opportunities.
It also puts you at risk of being forgotten, or just plain ignored. In a world that prizes excellence, the middle isn’t a safe place—it’s actually pretty dangerous.
So, here’s the real takeaway:
The greatest rewards are waiting for those who are willing to push through the dip and become the best.
It takes focus, it takes commitment, and it takes the guts to quit anything that doesn’t lead you closer to mastery.
